name: Mobutism
summary: Mobutism was the state ideology of Mobutu Sese Seko's Zaire, built on nationalism, revolution and authenticity. It rejected both capitalism and communism, justified a single party and a single chief as African tradition, and pursued cultural decolonisation through renaming and the abacost, while nationalising foreign business. In practice it served as a vehicle for a personal cult and kleptocratic rule.
scope: The official doctrine of the Popular Movement of the Revolution (MPR) in Zaire, 1967-1990s, as set out in the Manifesto of N'sele (1967) and the authenticité campaign (from 1971). It covers the regime's stated doctrine and the practices it justified; it excludes Lumumbism and the post-1997 Mobutist survivors such as the Union of Mobutist Democrats. No full text of the Manifesto was available, so it rests on descriptions of it.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Sources record no healthcare doctrine; the regime's collapse of public services and the labour-standards pledge point both ways.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: The Manifesto promised better labour standards, but nothing documents a wage-floor stance and the regime let real wages collapse.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Mobutism rejected capitalism as inauthentic and nationalised firms, though it left no worked-out case against markets.

public-ownership.rationale: Mobutu nationalised foreign firms and, after 1974, put Zairianized businesses under state control, though often to benefit his associates.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: No tax doctrine exists; a ruling elite that took large personal fortunes from the state would not favour taxing itself.

property-fundamental.rationale: Foreign and then Zairian-owned property was seized by decree in 1973-74, so property was overridable by the state.

cut-welfare.rationale: No documented welfare-cutting doctrine; the Manifesto promised improved labour standards, so cuts are not an adherent position.

worker-ownership.rationale: Ownership went to the state and to Zairian elites, not to workers; no workers-ownership strand is documented.

surveillance-ok.rationale: The regime relied on security services and presidential guard units to watch and repress opponents.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: The Manifesto condemned tribalism and regionalism, but no hate-speech law doctrine is documented.

strong-leader.rationale: Mobutu justified a single chief with the saying that in African tradition there are never two chiefs, and ruled by decree after suspending parliament.

state-harmful.rationale: The Manifesto expanded central state authority; the state was the vehicle of national revolution.

empower-police-military.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale is not about military spending, which this statement now asks about alone.

reviewHistory.rationale: The regime built up presidential guard and security units and ruled through the army chief turned president.
reviewHistory.author: claude-sonnet-5-5

reviewHistory.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale is not about military spending, which this statement now asks about alone.
reviewHistory.author: claude-opus-5-5

decide-locally.rationale: The Manifesto rejected regionalism and tribalism and enlarged central authority.

rehabilitation.rationale: The regime used public hangings and torture of rivals; no rehabilitative penal doctrine is documented.

more-religion-public.rationale: The regime curbed Christian churches, limited legal denominations to four and promoted devotion to Mobutu and the MPR in their place.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Authenticité addressed colonial cultural damage, but the sources document no race-redress programme.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Authenticité was a state campaign to restore Zairian culture and purge colonial European influences.

gradual-change.rationale: The Manifesto framed a national revolution, and the regime changed names, dress and calendars abruptly by decree.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Mobutism stressed independence and positive neutralism; Mobutu later resisted IMF scrutiny of corruption.

nation-first.rationale: Nationalism was one of the three pillars and independence was central, though Mobutu leaned on Western patrons.

limit-growth.rationale: The goal was economic independence and development, not limiting growth.

revolution-justified.rationale: The Manifesto called its programme a national revolution, though the revolution was top-down and the regime itself came from a coup.

central-planning.rationale: It rejected both capitalism and communism, and its state-run economy was ad hoc rather than planned.

socialized-markets.rationale: Ownership was passed to a favoured elite, not to workers or the public; Mobutism does not state this view.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The Manifesto expanded state authority over the economy and the state took control of nationalised enterprises.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Zairianization concentrated assets among associates; no small-property doctrine is documented.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: The MPR claimed all citizens as members, but no state-recognised employer-worker bodies are documented.

one-party-rule.rationale: The MPR was the only legal party; the Manifesto presented one-party rule as a way past Congo-crisis infighting.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Mobutu was a self-styled chief and father of the nation yet ruled as president; hereditary monarchy is not an adherent doctrine.

democracy-best.rationale: Mobutism framed competitive democracy as foreign to African tradition; elections were acclamation or single-candidate.

direct-votes.rationale: The regime held plebiscitary single-candidate votes, not citizen lawmaking; no direct-democracy doctrine.

workers-councils.rationale: The Manifesto rejected communism and put power in the party-state.

right-to-secede.rationale: The doctrine rejected regionalism and separatism, and the regime fought Katangan and Shaba movements.

natural-rulers.rationale: The claim that there are never two chiefs expresses rule by one natural chief, though not a formal doctrine of natural rulers.

political-violence-never.rationale: The regime hanged rivals publicly and killed Mulele; adherents do not hold political violence unjustified.

separate-church-state.rationale: The regime subordinated churches to the party and ran the MPR as a church-like body, rather than separating them.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Authority rested on Mobutu and the MPR, not scripture; Christianity was curbed.

private-courts-defense.rationale: State authority was to be expanded; private provision runs against that.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The Manifesto condemned tribalism and sought a single national identity above ethnic groups.

class-struggle-history.rationale: It rejected communism and held that neither Marxist nor capitalist schemes were authentic; class conflict was denied by the single-party line.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Stated goals were labour standards, not equality; the regime enriched an elite.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Authenticité was about culture and names, and the sources describe no land-rights programme for peoples; Zaire's land was nationalised in practice.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Authenticité was anti-colonial in culture, but no reparations demand is documented.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Official doctrine preached national solidarity, whatever elites practised.

duties-before-rights.rationale: The state demanded loyalty and party membership of every citizen, subordinating individual rights.

limit-population.rationale: The sources record no population policy under Mobutism; nothing stated either way.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Mobutism sought development and public works, not a rejection of industry.

restore-past-order.rationale: Authenticité revived ancestral customs selectively, with Mobutu saying he did not intend a blind return to them, while pursuing revolution and modernisation.

results-over-ideology.rationale: The N'Sele Manifesto presented the revolution as pragmatic, 'neither left nor right', although Mobutism itself became an enforced state creed; the stated doctrine leans toward judging by results.

direct-action.rationale: Change was from above; no support for grassroots direct action.

return-to-foraging.rationale: The doctrine aimed at national development, not abandoning civilisation.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Rejection of communism makes this a clear no.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Communist distribution principle rejected by the Manifesto.

profit-exploitation.rationale: The Manifesto rejected communism and Marxist analysis, so this Marxist claim is not adopted.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Anti-Marxist doctrine; Mobutu was a Western ally.

harm-principle.rationale: Authority was broad and personal; the state restricted dress, names, religion and politics.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Loyalty to the national party-community outranked individual rights.

exit-over-voice.rationale: A regime that banned parties and restricted dissent would not rank exit above the vote, though it also never framed the choice.

state-as-business.rationale: The state was run as a patronage network for the ruler, not as a service to customers.

media-academia-power.rationale: Mobutu controlled media and universities, as in the 1971 UNAZA merger.

organic-representation.rationale: The MPR claimed to embody every citizen from birth, a form of national rather than corporate representation.

total-state.rationale: All citizens were MPR members, and the party reached into dress, names, schools, churches and youth organisations.

national-rebirth.rationale: Authenticité aimed to rebuild national identity after colonial alienation.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Authority rested on loyalty to Mobutu, who rotated cabinets to keep clients dependent.

bound-labor.rationale: Nothing in Mobutism supports serfdom; it spoke of modernising labour standards and rejected tribal and customary hierarchies.

universal-morality.rationale: Authenticité held that values should be authentic to African culture, not universal; split inference.

single-common-good.rationale: The one-party state was justified as overcoming faction and serving national unity.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Mobutu had close ties with Israel at times, but no doctrine on this.

school-vouchers.rationale: The regime centralised education and made the Manifesto compulsory in schools.

economic-freedom.rationale: Political and economic life were state-directed.

rule-by-example.rationale: Propaganda presented Mobutu as a prophet and moral exemplar, though the regime also used force.

national-self-determination.rationale: Independence and nationalism were central, though applied only to the unitary national state.

force-without-un.rationale: Mobutism's neutralism did not settle this, and Zaire intervened in Angola with Western support but no stated doctrine on UN approval.

reason-over-faith.rationale: The cult of the leader gave faith-like devotion priority.

work-for-welfare.rationale: The sources describe no welfare scheme under the regime, so a work requirement is not an adherent question.

class-collaboration.rationale: The doctrine denied class conflict in favour of national unity under the party.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Authenticité sought to preserve and restore cultural heritage.

dominated-front.rationale: Positive neutralism and anti-colonial nationalism, though never a formal anti-Western front.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The doctrine was anti-colonial and opposed racial rule, though Mobutu cultivated ties with apartheid South Africa.

state-class-instrument.rationale: A Marxist claim rejected with communism.

elite-replacement.rationale: Mobutism's nationalism was anti-colonial rather than anti-immigrant conspiratorial; this theory appears nowhere in the sources.

proportional-representation.rationale: Single-party rule; no competing parties to apportion.

national-mission.rationale: The regime sought national revival at home and neutralism abroad rather than spreading its system to other peoples.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Eugenic policy is absent from Mobutism, and its custom-honouring authenticité would not support it.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: The regime killed opponents and shielded its forces.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The Manifesto expanded central authority over society and the economy.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: The doctrine opposed colonial racial hierarchy and has no racial-purity element in the sources.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Anti-colonial nationalism asserted African dignity, but the regime did not respect equal rights before law.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: The doctrine pushed one national identity, but nothing is documented on a civil code across religions.

restrict-conversion.rationale: The regime curbed churches but there is no documented conversion law.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: The regime fought the Catholic hold on schooling but the sources do not show a ban on religious instruction.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist formula; Mobutism rejected communism and framed its state-building differently.

consent-of-governed.rationale: The regime claimed consent through acclamation votes, but authority rested on the chief, not on genuine consent.

population-transfer.rationale: The regime did not adopt expulsions of minorities as doctrine, and the Manifesto condemned tribalism rather than singling out groups.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: The regime came to power by coup and used force against rivals.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: National unity, not competition, was the doctrine.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Mobutu banned all other parties in 1966, claiming national unity.

separated-powers.rationale: Mobutu suspended Parliament in 1966 and concentrated power in the president.

vanguard-party.rationale: Not a Marxist-Leninist doctrine; the MPR was a national party.

priority-to-poor.rationale: The Manifesto promised better labour standards, but the regime did not make the poor a doctrinal priority.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: The sources record no explanation of poverty in demographic terms.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: The Manifesto opposed tribalism and regionalism as threats to national unity.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Offices were filled by presidential appointment.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Mobutu ruled under a five-year state of exception after the coup and suspended Parliament.

party-controls-media.rationale: Under the MPR the media could in 1975 name only Mobutu.

party-commands-army.rationale: The army was personally led by Mobutu as party chief, but no party-over-state principle is documented.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Mobutu and his associates took huge personal fortunes.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: As a one-party doctrine, MPR decisions bound all members.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Mobutu was president and army chief, appointed the cabinet and reshuffled it 60 times.

clerical-rule.rationale: Authority lay in Mobutu and the MPR; clergy were subordinated.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Mobutu was re-elected in 1977 and 1984 in single-candidate votes and sought presidency for life in 1972.

recall-officials.rationale: Officials were removed by the president, not by voters.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Positive neutralism was stated, but Mobutu relied on US, French and Belgian backing.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Mobutism rejected communism and had no programme for universal ownership of homes.

people-in-arms.rationale: The regime relied on professional presidential guard units.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: The doctrine was built around Zaire's existing territory, with no reunification claim in the sources.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: The sources show no anti-intellectual line; the regime also made the Manifesto compulsory teaching at every school level.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Authenticité insisted African culture was no lesser than European and aimed at cultural disalienation.

death-penalty.rationale: The regime publicly hanged ex-prime minister Kimba and other rivals in 1966.

minority-language-support.rationale: The Manifesto opposed tribalism and regionalism.

religious-exemptions.rationale: The state recognised only four religious bodies and declared others illegal.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: The state dictated dress, names and forms of address.

constituent-assembly.rationale: The constitution was drawn up and rewritten under presidential control.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: The Manifesto presented one-party rule as pragmatic for national development.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Mobutu was confirmed by popular single-candidate votes in 1970, 1977 and 1984, a plebiscitary form.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Mobutu took large shares of the budget; an independent bank would limit that.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Nationalisation was justified by national economic independence.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Mobutism rejected communism and the Soviets; the sources give no analysis of Soviet economics.

collective-defense.rationale: Mobutu relied on Western allies, but no formal alliance doctrine is documented.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: The state dissolved church youth groups, forced JMPR committees into seminaries and limited legal denominations to four.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Mobutu was both head of state and leader of the sole party.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: The regime fought Katanga/Shaba separatists, and the Manifesto condemned separatism.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Centralisation and a unitary state were basic aims.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Propaganda cast Mobutu as messiah and prophet, though not of hereditary divine descent.

character-from-environment.rationale: Authenticité stressed African culture shaping people, but the sources do not take a side on nature versus upbringing.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Mobutu suspended parliament and ruled by decree under a state of exception.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Power was concentrated in a single ruler.

leader-cult.rationale: Mobutu was styled Father of the Nation and Savior of the People, with images replacing crucifixes in the party's propaganda.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Not a socialist state in these terms.

women-must-cover.rationale: Authenticité created a female national dress, but the sources show no law requiring full covering.

common-currency.rationale: The currency was renamed the zaire as a national symbol.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: The Manifesto opposed tribalism and regionalism.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: A Marxist claim rejected along with communism.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Economic independence was a goal, but not a closed bloc.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Mobutu styled himself a chief but abolished no titles; the sources give no doctrine on hereditary rank.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Authenticité aimed to centre national culture and the Manifesto was taught in all schools.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Authenticité was explicitly anti-colonial, aiming at mental decolonisation.

patriotic-education.rationale: From 1969 the Manifesto was mandatory teaching at every school level.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: The sources show no racial-preference policy in Zaire or position on abolishing one.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: The Manifesto rejected capitalism as alien but did not predict its collapse.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Mobutu cut cultural colonial ties, though Belgium and France remained patrons.

delink-world-market.rationale: Zaire stayed integrated into the world economy via copper exports and Western aid.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: The state itself regulated names, religion and dress.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Rights were subordinate to the leader; parliament was suspended.

elective-rulers.rationale: Rulers were nominally confirmed by plebiscite.

minority-veto.rationale: The doctrine stressed unity and a single chief.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Dissent was suppressed; Mobutu held that rule rested in a single chief.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Mobutu suspended Parliament in 1966; later legislatures were elected by acclamation.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Animal welfare is absent from the sources on the doctrine.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: The MPR claimed every citizen from birth and required participation.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: A Gramscian claim absent from Mobutism, which denied class division.

party-own-road.rationale: Positive neutralism and the claim that the revolution owed nothing to Moscow or Peking.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Mobutu's authenticité and the 1967 N'Sele Manifesto proclaimed economic independence and Zairianisation, though in practice the regime relied heavily on Western aid and loans; the doctrine leans toward self-reliance.

return-lost-territory.rationale: The sources document no irredentist claims by Zaire.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: The sources do not show antifascism in the doctrine, which had its own constitution-making under Mobutu.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Mobutism condemned communism by name but the sources show no statement on fascism as an equivalent.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Authenticité renamed colonial-era places and removed colonial symbols.

military-guardian-role.rationale: The regime itself was an army-born order and relied on military and guard units.

office-by-exam.rationale: Offices were filled by patronage and reshuffled for loyalty.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Officials answered to the president, not voters.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Parliament was suspended and later elected by acclamation; the ruler controlled budget.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Nationalisation hit foreign property, but no land rule is documented.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: The sources show no critique of consumption, though the regime itself was marked by elite extravagance.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Zaire backed Angolan rebel groups against the MPLA.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: The question of bloc discipline did not arise for non-aligned Zaire in the sources.

corporate-influence.rationale: Mobutism opposed foreign firms but the sources do not frame it as lobbying influence.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: The sources describe no family-incentive policy in Zaire.

job-guarantee.rationale: The Manifesto promised better labour standards but no guarantee of employment is documented.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: The Manifesto and loyalty to the leader were compulsory civic duties.

non-intervention.rationale: The MPR doctrine of positive neutralism proclaimed non-interference between the blocs, although Zaire sent forces into Angola and Chad; the stated position leans toward non-intervention.

public-access-to-information.rationale: The media were controlled and opposition suppressed.

informal-organisation.rationale: A single mass party claimed all citizens.

religious-nation.rationale: The nation was defined by authentic national identity, not religion, and the state stood above churches.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: The Manifesto opposed regionalism; the centre controlled revenues.

defeat-communism.rationale: Mobutu was a Cold War anti-communist backed by the US, France and Belgium.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: The sources describe no delivery model for public services.

religion-illusion.rationale: The regime did not call religion illusion; it tried to replace Christianity with a Mobutist faith.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: A Marxist claim; the Manifesto rejected capitalism as alien without crediting it as progressive.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Names and place names were Africanised, but no loanword purge is documented.

majority-settlement.rationale: The doctrine opposed regionalism but the sources show no settlement policy.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: The Manifesto rejected both as inauthentic and called its programme a national revolution; the slogan was neither left nor right.

historical-land-claim.rationale: The sources show no historical or religious land-claim doctrine in Mobutism.

suppress-opposition.rationale: All other parties were banned in 1966 and rivals were hanged or killed.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Authenticité aimed at undoing colonial structures.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Not a religious-law doctrine; Mobutu claimed his own authority.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: A modern academic theory absent from the sources on the doctrine.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: The MPR slogan was neither left nor right, later neither left, right nor centre.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Propaganda claimed divine sanction for Mobutu, but doctrine located authority in the nation and its founder.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: A modern workplace question with no basis in the sources.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The regime depended on its army.

rich-first.rationale: The regime enriched elites first, but no stated doctrine of it.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: The Manifesto called for positive neutralism.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Mobutu's son leads the Mobutist party today, but the doctrine did not propose dynastic succession.

domination-women-nature.rationale: An ecofeminist claim absent from the sources.

reification.rationale: A Marxist concept the doctrine did not use, having rejected Marxist analysis.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: The ruler was above law and governed by decree.

open-government-data.rationale: The regime hid state finances; IMF auditors found corruption.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Deliberation by random citizens does not fit a regime based on acclamation and presidential appointment.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: The regime concentrated wealth; not an adherent view.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: The regime promoted devotion to Mobutu, not atheism.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: The doctrine centralised power and opposed ethnic regionalism.

term-limits.rationale: Mobutu sought presidency for life and was re-elected repeatedly.

vote-delegation.rationale: Liquid delegation conflicts with a regime built on acclamation and a single leader.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Long-term risk policy appears nowhere in the sources on the doctrine.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Foreign-owned firms were nationalised and then Zairianized in 1973-74, a stronger form of control over foreign ownership.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: The Manifesto tied political independence to economic independence as a stated goal.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Authenticité sought to restore a precolonial African tradition as the basis of national identity.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Zairianization in 1973-74 transferred foreign-owned firms to Zairian citizens as a central economic policy.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: The Manifesto claimed to rise above both capitalism and communism and gave no role to working-class power; rule was by a single chief and party.

municipal-property.rationale: The Manifesto set central authority and national ownership of key assets, not municipal ownership.

confederal-coordination.rationale: The doctrine stressed central authority and a single party over local autonomy.

family-wage.rationale: The Manifesto promised better labour standards but the sources document no family-wage stance.

person-over-state.rationale: Mobutism's cult of the leader and party-state placed the nation and chief above individuals, though the sources record no explicit doctrine on persons as means.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Authenticité appealed to African cultural and spiritual tradition against colonial materialism, though the state also restricted organised religion.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Mobutism stressed African authenticity and cultural identity, not organising politically by race.

racial-pride.rationale: Authenticité asserted pride in African heritage and identity against colonial inferiority.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Mobutism posed as positive neutralism but backed foreign interventions in the region, and the sources give no doctrine on defensive-only force.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Authenticité promoted African cultural unity and Zairian identity, but Zaire's own borders and many languages mean the regime upheld colonial-era borders, not linguistic unification.

communal-electorates.rationale: The regime defended a single party and a single chief as authentic, and rejected ethnic and regional politics, so separate community electorates were incompatible.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Mobutu justified central authority by the Katanga and Kasai secessions and Western or Soviet scheming, and invoked outside plots against Zaire's unity.

arms-reduction.rationale: The regime relied on a large army and Western arms support and stressed national security, though it professed positive neutralism.

capital-controls.rationale: The regime nationalised foreign firms (Zairianization) and rejected capitalism, while foreign exchange and capital flows were state-controlled.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: The regime centralised force in the army and security services and suppressed rival armed groups; central authority is a Manifesto principle.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Under the single-party MPR, unions were subordinate to the party; independent bargaining is incompatible with one-party doctrine.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: No such scheme is documented; the regime's economic management ran against targeted income support.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: The Manifesto's positive neutralism and rejection of both capitalism and communism fit calls to change the global order; stated vaguely.

smash-state-machine.rationale: The Manifesto stressed central authority and the single party took over the existing state, not smashing it.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: A single party and a single chief as tradition leave no room for communities choosing their own systems.

nature-as-capital.rationale: No documented doctrine; the regime treated natural resources as sources of state and personal revenue.

sacred-nation.rationale: The Manifesto's nationalism and the cult of the leader made the nation the central object of loyalty, though not formally religious.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Authenticity stressed African identity, but no stance on a shared human nature is documented.

public-service-media.rationale: The regime used state media as an arm of the MPR and a vehicle for the personality cult, the opposite of independent public media.

religions-one-truth.rationale: The doctrine promoted authenticity and indigenous belief over imported Christian names and forms, but did not state a view on whether religions share one truth.

workers-own-party.rationale: The doctrine made the MPR the single party of the whole nation, and independent parties, including workers' ones, were barred.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Authenticite restricted and regulated churches while the MPR acted as a quasi-religion; the sources give no doctrine of equal legal standing between interpretations.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: The Manifesto rejected multiparty competition and presented a single party and chief as African tradition, with one-candidate votes.

premarital-sex.rationale: Authenticite promoted supposedly traditional values, but the sources record no sexual-morality doctrine; adherents could go either way.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: The MPR had official women's organisations but the sources record no equality agencies as doctrine.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Authenticité restricted Christian practice and renamed Christians and Churches, subordinating religion to the national doctrine.

defend-planned-state.rationale: The N'sele Manifesto rejected both capitalism and communism, so a planned state was not defended as such.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: The Manifesto and doctrine stress central authority and national unity against tribalism, and the regime crushed Katangan and other regional movements.

close-ties-china.rationale: Mobutu recognised Beijing in 1972 and visited China, but the regime stayed firmly aligned with the West, so this is a weak inference.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: The Manifesto rejected both capitalism and communism and nationalised foreign firms, but nothing documents a doctrine of resource compensation owed to all.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Mobutism justified a single party and a single chief as African tradition, with the leader as father of the nation dealing with the people through the MPR rather than rival parties or independent unions.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: The MPR was the only legal party and authenticité restricted church influence, so politics along religious lines was not permitted.

national-resource-control.rationale: The Manifesto's economic nationalism and Zairianization and the 1970s nationalisation of copper mining put the country's resources under national control.

missingStatements.text: A country should replace foreign-sounding personal and place names with indigenous ones as part of throwing off colonial influence.
missingStatements.rationale: Authenticité banned Christian names, renamed cities and the country, and Mobutu changed his own name.
missingStatements.declined: The audit's own answer to purge-loanwords is neutral; renaming is a narrow authenticite policy that does not generalise.

missingStatements.text: The national government should assign foreign-owned businesses to citizens of the country by decree.
missingStatements.rationale: Zairianization transferred foreign firms to Zairians in 1973-74.
missingStatements.declined: Zairianization is a narrow historical policy; foreign-takeover-block and public-ownership cover the contested ground.

notes: Official doctrine and regime practice diverge sharply: sources document kleptocracy and repression under a rhetoric of national revolution. Answers follow the stated doctrine where it speaks and regime practice otherwise, with most untouched topics left as low-confidence inferences.
